headline: Subcommittee voted 2-0 to forward portable weapon detection unit proposal to full School Committee as a progress report.
summary: The subcommittee heard a presentation on the District-Wide Safety Committee's safety initiatives, including ALICE drills, emergency evacuation routes, and Go Bags. Officials discussed portable weapon detection units, estimated at $40,196.50 for two units and $59,759.80 for three units, and agreed to bring the proposal and supporting data to the full School Committee.
decisions: Voted to present the weapon detection unit matter to the whole Committee and accept it as a report of progress, passing 2-0 with 1 absent.

Ms. Breault-Guibicki explained that the District-Wide Safety Committee is comprised of
representatives from Safety, lnformation Technology (lT), and Facilities. The committee held its
first meeting on Octobe r 29,2025, and meets monthly throughout the year. The committee

Support Services, McKinney-Vento, Safety, lT, and Facilities. ln addition, the committee meets
weekly on Wednesdays with Facilities staff and collaborates with Management lnformation

She discussed the committee's purpose and mission, which are to foster equitable and inclusive
learning environments throughout the district while engaging families in promoting student
belonging and social-emot¡onal well-being. The Safety Committee's primary purpose is to create
and maintain a physically and emotionally safe environment for all students, staff, and families
by identifying safety concerns, implementing preventative measures, and promoting awareness
of safety practices.

Ms. Breault-Guibicki concluded her presentation by discussing enhanced safety planning and the
potential use of portable weapon detection units. Based on a quote received the previous year,
the estimated cost was approximately S40,196.50 for two units and 559,759.80 for three units.
That cost could change this Year.
Ms. Crocker-Roberge stated that she had made two visits to Lawrence High School with
administrators, LPD representatives, security personnel, and the Safety Coordinator to observe
the portable weapon detection units and discuss the implementation and rollout process. The
group also discussed how the Lawrence community, staff, and students were notified about the
implementation. She explained that, if Lowell were to move forward with the technology, the
district would initially conduct a trial with a small group of students and staff. These units would
also be available to be used at night for school sponsored events.
Ms. Crocker-Roberge also provided an update on additional safety measures recently
implemented by the district. These included the purchase of additional security cameras and
two-way radios. She noted that LPS staff members have been CPR trained and certified and are
able to provide training to additional staff. The district has also purchased additional LifeVac
anti-choking devices for use in schools.

Ms. Crocker-Roberge noted that the safety budget is not as large as it was last year and stated
that the district may need to begin with two portable weapon detection units.
Mr. Lay asked whether school nurses had received CPR training. Ms. Breault-Guibicki responded
affirmatively.
Mr. Lay then asked about the district's current protocol for responding to intruders. Ms. Breault-
Guibicki explained that all exterior doors are secured and are not permitted to be propped
open. She stated that School Resource Officers (SROs) conduct daily perimeter checks of all
exterior doors to ensure that they remain secure.
Ms. Martin expressed concern that implementing weapon detection technology may be a
significant step without additional information regarding the need for it. She requested that the
Committee receive data related to school safety and incidents involving weapons at the next
School Committee meeting to assist members in evaluating the proposal.
Ms. Crocker-Roberge clarified that the consideration of portable weapon detection units was
not prompted by any specific incident and that the initiative is being pursued as a proactive
safety measure. She stated that this technology has become a new standard and baseline for
enhancing the safety of students and staff. She offered to provide the requested data and noted
that several school districts currently using weapon detection units have reported a significant
decrease in safety-related incidents.
Chairperson Martin moved to present this to the whole Committee and to accept this as a
report of progress; the motion was seconded by Mr. Lay. The mot¡on passed with 2 yeas, 1
absent (Ms. Delrossi).
Ms. Crocker-Roberge then addressed agenda item #2. She explained that the district's standard
practice is to conduct a comprehensive debrief following major events, reviewing all parts of the
response and identified areas for improvement. She stated that, based on the findings from the
debrief, changes were made to the district's procedures and subsequently implemented during
another major event that happened in the city.
